title: Integral duality and a finite extension of coefficient fields
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ use the completed coefficient sheaves $\widehat R_X$ and $\widehat S_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and their ordinary sheaves of modules. Write
$$T_{S/R}K=K\widehat\otimes_R^L S$$
for the strict-tower integral scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], identified on derived-complete inputs with ordinary derived tensor $K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}\widehat S_X$ by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. It is exact and preserves the integral bounded constructible categories of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Internal Hom means the ambient derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $\omega_{X,R}$ and $\omega_{X,S}$ are the integral dualizing objects [prop-coef-integral-dualizing], and $D_{X,R}$ and $D_{X,S}$ are the ambient integral Verdier duals [thm-coef-integral-verdier].

For $K,M\in D^b_c(X,R)$ there are canonical isomorphisms
$$
u_{L/E}:T_{S/R}\omega_{X,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,S},
\qquad
v_{K,M}:T_{S/R}R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(K,M)
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat S_X}(T_{S/R}K,T_{S/R}M),
$$
and consequently
$$
\beta_{L/E,K}:T_{S/R}D_{X,R}K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,S}(T_{S/R}K).
$$
They commute with evaluation and with the canonical map $K\to D_{X,R}D_{X,R}K$. They are compatible with finite coefficient quotients [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], the identity extension, and composition of finite field extensions, including the tensor associators.

proof.text:
Put $\mathcal R=\widehat R_X$ and $\mathcal S=\widehat S_X$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $\mathcal S$ is finite free over $\mathcal R$, completed tensor agrees with ordinary derived scalar extension on derived-complete inputs, and the output is derived $v$-complete. Ordinary derived scalar extension is exact by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Put $A_n=R/t^n$, $B_n=S/t^nS=S/v^{en}$; the equality of ideals and finite freeness of $B_n/A_n$ are in [lem-coef-finite-free-extension]. On flat-term K-flat representatives, extension and subsequent quotient are computed by ordinary tensor, and remain K-flat after extension by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Balancing gives
$$(T_{S/R}K)_{en}\cong (B_n)_X\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}K_n,\qquad K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal R}(A_n)_X.$$
These are identifications of the quotient diagrams, since both successive quotient maps send $s\otimes x$ to its quotient class.

source.place: first paragraph: exactness and cofinal reductions; tensor calculation also uses Stacks Tags 06YY, 07A4 and 0G7E

proof.text: The existing constructibility theorem [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] applies to this same strict-tower scalar extension and gives $T_{S/R}K\in D^b_c(X,S)$, with the definition [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Here is the uniform Tor bound used in the blueprint: choose $[a,b]$ containing the cohomology of $K_1$. Then [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] gives Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ for every $K_n$. For any degree-zero $(B_n)_X$-module $N$, balancing identifies $((B_n)_X\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}K_n)\otimes^L_{(B_n)_X}N$ with $K_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}\operatorname{Res}N$, whose cohomology vanishes outside $[a,b]$. The definition [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] therefore gives the same bound after extension. For an intervening level put $C_m=S/v^m$ and choose $en\ge m$. For every degree-zero $(C_m)_X$-module $N$, the formula $((K_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}(B_n)_X)\otimes^L_{(B_n)_X}(C_m)_X)\otimes^L_{(C_m)_X}N\cong K_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}\operatorname{Res}N$ gives vanishing outside $[a,b]$, with no flatness assumption on $B_n\to C_m$. The quotient identifications are normalized, and [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] reconstructs them. This verifies that the preservation theorem is being used for the same completed functor and the same uniformly bounded category, rather than for a different notion of integral coefficients.

source.place: first paragraph after displayed reductions: constructibility and uniform Tor bounds

proof.text:
Choose an integer $d\ge0$ with $\dim X\le d$, using finite dimensionality [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Then [prop-coef-integral-dualizing] applies over both coefficient fields: it constructs $\omega_{X,R}$ and $\omega_{X,S}$ as total limits of coherent finite dualizing systems and identifies their reductions. For every $n$, [lem-coef-finite-free-extension] gives the canonical counit-defined isomorphism
$$(B_n)_X\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}\omega_{X,A_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,B_n}.$$
Its quotient compatibility gives the transition squares at the cofinal exponents $en$. To specify a map on the full $S$-tower, put $C_m=S/v^m$ and use the quotient $B_m=S/v^{em}\to C_m$. Tensor the displayed map for $n=m$ with $(C_m)_X$ over $(B_m)_X$, then compose with the counit-defined isomorphism $\omega_{X,B_m}\otimes^L_{(B_m)_X}(C_m)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,C_m}$ of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]. This gives
$$\omega_{X,A_m}\otimes^L_{(A_m)_X}(C_m)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,C_m}.$$
For $m'\ge m$, the two routes from $B_{m'}$ to $C_m$ are $B_{m'}\to B_m\to C_m$ and $B_{m'}\to C_{m'}\to C_m$. The finite-free comparison commutes with $B_{m'}\to B_m$, and the identity and composition equations of the finite dualizing quotient comparisons identify the composites along these two routes. The source identifications use the normalized reductions $\omega_{X,A_{m'}}\otimes^L_{(A_{m'})_X}(A_m)_X\cong\omega_{X,A_m}$ from the proposition. Thus these maps respect every transition, including exponents not divisible by $e$, and retain the counit normalization.

The simultaneous derived coefficient-extension and evaluation/mate models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] realize the counit-defined comparisons and their quotient composites of Step 3 as a coherent morphism on the full tower indexed by $m\ge1$. The first input systems are cartesian, since their quotient comparisons are the normalization isomorphisms; thus the stated restriction on the evaluation clause is met. All components are isomorphisms by [lem-coef-finite-free-extension] and [lem-coef-finite-dualizing], so the coherent morphism is an equivalence. Restriction along $\mathcal S\to(C_m)_X$ puts it in the constant-ring tower category. Applying the functor $R\lim$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] gives an isomorphism. Its source tower is $m\mapsto\operatorname{Res}^S_m(\omega_{X,R}\otimes^L_{\mathcal R}(C_m)_X)$, using the coherent reduction identifications of [prop-coef-integral-dualizing] and tensor balancing. Its limit is exactly the strict-tower scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies it with $T_{S/R}\omega_{X,R}$. Its target limit is the actual $\omega_{X,S}$ of the proposition; [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] identifies its projections. This constructs $u_{L/E}$ on the full tower, without a separate assertion about changing the index of a derived limit. Functoriality of the simultaneous models and of $R\lim$ gives naturality, and applying them to the finite counit diagrams gives counit compatibility.

source.place: third paragraph: coherent tower maps and their derived limit

proof.text:
For the completed ring-sheaf map $\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$, the module adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] with identity underlying topos is extension of scalars left adjoint to restriction. Its left adjoint is exact: after forgetting scalars a finite free basis identifies it with a finite direct sum. Let $P$ be a complex representing $K$ and let $I$ be an $\mathcal S$-K-injective representative of $N\in D(\mathcal S)$. Exactness lets $\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}P$ represent scalar extension of $K$. Then [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] shows that $\operatorname{Res}I$ is $\mathcal R$-K-injective. Applying the ordinary module adjunction to each Hom-complex degree, on every slice site, gives
$$\operatorname{Res}\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}P,I)
=\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{\mathcal R}(P,\operatorname{Res}I).$$
The derived internal-Hom model [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] thus identifies
$$\operatorname{Res}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal S\otimes^L_{\mathcal R}K,N)
\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal R}(K,\operatorname{Res}N).$$
The formulas in this identification are $g\mapsto(x\mapsto g(1\otimes x))$ and $f\mapsto(s\otimes x\mapsto s f(x))$, so the identification respects evaluation.

source.place: fourth paragraph: extension-restriction adjunction; Stacks Tags 03D7 and 08BJ

proof.text: Define $v_{K,M}$ to be the tensor-Hom transpose of scalar-extended evaluation, using the closed derived tensor-Hom calculus [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and its global Hom identification [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]; the strong tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. After restriction of scalars, Step 5 identifies its target with $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal R}(K,\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}M)$. Choose a finite free basis $s_1,\ldots,s_r$ for $\mathcal S$ as an $\mathcal R$-module, which exists by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Both sides become $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal R}(K,M)^{\oplus r}$: a finite sum of K-injective resolutions is K-injective, since maps from an acyclic complex into it are tuples of null-homotopic maps; Hom into that finite sum is the finite sum of Hom complexes. The component $s_i\otimes f$ maps to $x\mapsto s_i\otimes f(x)$, so the matrix of the comparison is the identity. Restriction detects quasi-isomorphisms, since it keeps the underlying abelian sheaves and their cohomology. Thus $v_{K,M}$ is an isomorphism without a site-perfectness hypothesis on $K$. The corollary [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom] and Step 2 place both sides in the integral bounded constructible category. The basis is used only to test invertibility, not to define the map.

source.place: fourth paragraph: finite-basis test of the evaluation-defined comparison; Stacks Tags 08J9, 08JA and 07A4

proof.text:
Set $\beta_{L/E,K}=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal S}(T_{S/R}K,u_{L/E})\circ v_{K,\omega_{X,R}}$. The integral Verdier theorem [thm-coef-integral-verdier] identifies its source and target with the displayed integral duals. By the definition of $v$ by transposition, the composite pairing after $\beta$ is $u_{L/E}\circ T_{S/R}(\operatorname{ev}_K)$, under the scalar tensor comparison. Applying the same identity to $D_{X,R}K$ and transposing in $T_{S/R}K$ gives
$$D_{X,S}(\beta_{L/E,K})\circ\delta_{T_{S/R}K}
=\beta_{L/E,D_{X,R}K}\circ T_{S/R}(\delta_K).$$
Both sides are maps from $T_{S/R}K$ to $D_{X,S}(T_{S/R}D_{X,R}K)$; their transposes are that same evaluation pairing. This proves compatibility with the actual canonical double-dual map, not merely with an abstract biduality isomorphism.

source.place: fifth paragraph: beta, evaluation and double-dual compatibility

proof.text: For every $m\ge1$ put $C_m=S/v^m$. By Steps 3-4 the reduction of $u$ is the finite-free comparison at $A_m\to B_m=S/v^{em}$ followed by the quotient comparison at $B_m\to C_m$ of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]. The corollary [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom] identifies reductions of the ambient integral Homs with the finite Homs by evaluation-defined isomorphisms. After its $A_m$ comparison, use the finite-free internal-Hom isomorphism of [lem-coef-finite-free-extension], then the quotient internal-Hom isomorphism of [thm-coef-finite-hom] for the $L$-coefficient exponents $em\ge m$. All inputs have finite Tor amplitude by Step 2 (and the dualizing proposition when needed). Tensor reassociation sends $s\otimes(f\otimes x)$ to $(s\otimes f)\otimes(1\otimes x)$, so this composite has exactly the evaluation transpose obtained by reducing the definition of $v$. Uniqueness of transpose identifies the two maps. For $m'\ge m$, both reductions factor through $B_{m'}\to B_m\to C_m$ and $B_{m'}\to C_{m'}\to C_m$ as in Step 3. The composition equations of the finite quotient Hom and dualizing nodes, and the cofinal quotient squares of the finite-free node, therefore give the commuting reduction square. This proves compatibility at every positive quotient exponent; it does not require $C_m$ to be free over $A_m$. Composition with $u$ gives the assertion for $\beta$, and [thm-coef-integral-verdier] identifies the reduced actual double-dual map with the finite one. These operations are performed on the simultaneous evaluation models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], so equality of integral maps is not inferred merely from equality of their finite reductions.

For nested valuation rings $R\subset S\subset U$, use the associator
$$U\otimes_S^L(S\otimes_R^LK)\xrightarrow{\sim}U\otimes_R^LK.$$
Here tensor denotes tensor of the corresponding completed sheaves; by the finite-free comparison these are the completed functors on the inputs under consideration. On flat-term K-flat representatives the associator is $u\otimes(s\otimes x)\mapsto us\otimes x$; the derived tensor models of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] compute it. For $u_{-/ -}$, choose a common cofinal exponent in the three coefficient towers, using the product of the two ramification indices. There the composition equation is the finite coefficient composition equation of [lem-coef-finite-free-extension]. At any other exponent extend it by the quotient maps of Step 3; the composition equations of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing] identify the two routes through the larger exponent. These are equations of the simultaneous coherent system maps of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], before applying the functor $R\lim$, so they give the integral composition equation. For $v$, the iterated comparison and the direct comparison both transpose to $u\otimes s\otimes f\otimes x\mapsto us\otimes f(x)$. Uniqueness of transpose from the closed tensor-Hom calculus gives equality, including the associator. The same equation for $\beta$ follows by its definition and the equation for $u$. For an identity extension all these formulas are the unit maps, and $u$ is the identity by its finite-level construction. Hence the comparisons satisfy identity and composition compatibilities with no basis choices.

source.place: fifth paragraph associator and final paragraph: identity and composition
